messages:
sara: 👀 noticing elevated 5xx and p99 latency from eu-south-1 for both Hosted API and several Dedicated pools. Radar shows ELB 502/504 spike + STS request throttling. Root cause likely a regional AWS control-plane/backplane issue. paging eng-oncall and infra.
pagerduty: Incident triggered: P1 - region eu-south-1 elevated 5xx/latency affecting hosted + dedicated. Escalation -> eng-oncall, infra, ops_lead.
infra-bot: Metric alert: elb_5xx_rate > 5% for 5m in eu-south-1. STS_429_rate > 1% for 5m. Links: https://metrics.local/alerts/2253001234
mike: taking this. on-call now. what's the observed customer impact? any VIPs on Dedicated pools?
sara: several Dedicated pools: rp-ded-eu-101 and rp-ded-eu-118 showing retries and queue growth. A handful of high-traffic hosted keys reporting slow responses and 502s. sales-support, heads up for top 3 customers on EU region.
eng-oncall: can you post the snapshot of `kubectl get pods` for runtime in eu-south-1? I want to check for crashloops or restart loops.
sara: pasted logs from control plane and ELB:
```
ELB: 2026-03-15T10:12:22Z elb-request 502 45.3ms target/10.0.1.23 "POST /v1/generate"
STS: ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded
Runtime: no crashloops, pod CPU high and connection errors to metadata/sts endpoint
```
mike: STS throttling suggests auth token vendor (AWS STS) is rate limiting our IAM calls. We're making frequent AssumeRole calls per request for some Dedicated pools due to token caching bug in last deploy.
carla: oh — we shipped a change yesterday that reduced token cache TTL for security. that might have regressed under load.
ops_lead: priority: mitigate user impact first. suggested path: reduce STS calls (rollback if needed), route new traffic away from eu-south-1 to eu-west-1 fallback pool, increase NLB capacity if possible, and enable short-term token fallback using cached credentials.
mike: rolling back token TTL change now for affected hosts. patch command:
```
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/runtime TOKEN_TTL=3600 --context=eu-south-1
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/runtime -n runtime --context=eu-south-1
```
infra-bot: Started: route update to send new requests to eu-west-1 for hosted: executing traffic-reroute job.
eng-oncall: also enabling routing policy fallback in the control plane: switching priority order for region selection for global customers.
carla: sales-support contacting top customers now. drafting message for status page.
sales-support: posting to status page draft:
"We're investigating elevated errors and latency in our eu-south-1 region. Some API requests may fail or see increased latency. We're routing new traffic to alternate regions where possible and working on fixes. Updates in 15m."
infra-bot: routing job log:
```
JOB_ID=reroute-2253001234
status: started
affected_targets: hosted-api-eu-south-1, rp-ded-eu-101, rp-ded-eu-118
action: set preferred_regions=[eu-west-1,eu-north-1]
```
mike: monitoring after rollback and reroute. initial signs: 5xx rate for ELB dropping from 12% -> 6% after 3 minutes. STS throttles still present but trending down.
sara: customers on dedicated pools seeing partial recovery, some queued requests still timing out. any temporary rate-limiting we should add on our side to reduce retries?
eng-oncall: yes, add client-side jittered exponential backoff and drop aggressive retries for 30m window. Patching in-flight config for retry policy:
```
PATCH /config/retry
{"max_retries":2, "base_backoff_ms":200}
```
pagerduty: Reminder: please post a customer-facing update and assign postmortem owner.
ops_lead: assigning postmortem to carla and eng-oncall. timeline + action items due EOD. we also need a rollback alert in deploy pipeline to prevent re-deploy of token-ttl change.
carla: creating incident ticket now. linking dashboards and logs. collecting affected API keys and Dedicated pool IDs.
sales-support: notified customers A, B, C (top EU customers). they're monitoring. one asked for private status update; will provide.
mike: current state: routing fallback active, token-ttl rolled back, retry policy tightened. still seeing occasional latency spikes but 5xx stabilizing ~1-2%.
infra-bot: Auto-check: all critical health checks passing in eu-west-1. eu-south-1 still degraded but stable.
eng-oncall: handoff incoming to night oncall in 40m. will document mitigation steps and where to revert if rollback causes side-effects.
sara: thanks team. please keep updates short. if anything regresses, escalate immediately.
carla: incident routed to postmortem board: https://pm.local/incidents/2253001234
ops_lead: decision log: root cause = combination of STS regional throttling + recent token cache TTL change increasing token exchange frequency. Mitigations: rollback TTL change, traffic reroute, retry policy change. Long term actions: implement token caching invariant across Dedicated pools, add circuit-breaker for STS errors, and add deploy guard to prevent reducing token TTL below X without perf test.
mike: marking incident as mitigated. continuing to monitor for 1hr. will update when resolved.
pagerduty: Incident status: Mitigated -> Monitoring. oncall mikes to update if reoccur.
carla: postmortem owner noted. will post draft within 24h.
eng-oncall: handing off to night oncall @mike-night in 35m. keeping watchlist and runbook links attached.
mike: oncall handover: state=monitoring, reroute job active, rollback applied, key impacted pools: rp-ded-eu-101/rp-ded-eu-118, suggested next steps if error spikes: 1) add temporary cap on assume-role calls via local token cache, 2) temporarily disable dedicated pool autoscaling to limit churn.
sara: closing thread for now. final update when fully resolved.
